To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the magnetization direction in Co nanowires is modulated periodically along the wire, with a modulation period of 1.4 μm, (ii) the modulation period depends on the wire diameter, (iii) the modulation period can be changed by applying a magnetic field, and (iv) the modulation is a result of the competition between crystal anisotropies and the demagnetization energy.
we have shown that the magnetization in cobalt nanowires is not uniformly oriented, but exhibits a spatial modulation of the magnetization angle with respect to the wire axis.
the crystal anisotropic energy and the demagnetization energy of cobalt nanowires are in balance and lead to a periodic modulation of the magnetization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the magnetic and structural properties of Co nanowires.
the magnetic properties of Co nanowires with different lengths, diameters and crystallographic orientations.
the magnetization dynamics of single crystalline nanowires.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetism of cobalt nanowires is a very rich and complex phenomenon, with many different aspects that have been explored in the last decade.
the magnetic properties of the cobalt nanowires are dominated by the competition between demagnetization energy and crystal anisotropies.
the magnetic properties of Co nanowires can only be understood in the context of the interplay between the magnetocrystalline anisotropy energy, the shape anisotropy, and the dipolar interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic properties can be tailored by controlling the diameter of the nanowires.
the periodic modulation of the magnetization direction can be controlled by the wire diameter.
we can prepare Co nanowires with the c-axis perpendicular to the wire-axis and that we can modulate the magnetization direction by a magnetic field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetic anisotropy of a single crystal can be used to control the magnetization direction in the nanowire.
this modulation is not a static phenomenon but is rather a dynamic one.
the magnetic properties of the nanowires can be controlled by the wire diameter and by the wire length.
